rules: Same ratchet-down-only policy as the live site's tool/page-budget.json (see its 'rules' field): any PR that reduces exampleSite page weight must lower maxPageBytes (or a tightened override, or maxCssBundleBytes) in the same PR — reclaimed bytes are banked, never slack. Home has NO override — it must fit the default budget for real. Ratchet history: Task 13 first trimmed home from 137,669/138,334 B to under 135,000 B (pricing teaser simplified to a plans-only summary, redundant <title> fixed), then narrowing fraunces-roman.woff2 (wght axis + opsz pinned per the typography owner's verdict — see tool/subset_fonts.sh) dropped every page ~29 KB and funded the 135,000 → 123,000 ratchet (~15% over the heaviest regular page, same margin methodology as the live site's own baseline+15%). The per-page-kind CSS split was later removed as an architecture smell (page-oriented styling): the single cached main.css bundle costs every page ~7.7 KB more on FIRST load in exchange for zero per-navigation CSS and a page-agnostic section/component architecture. Product-owner ruling 2026-07-26: the default HOLDS at 123,000 (heaviest regular page 113,839 B, 8% headroom) — recalibrating it up would hand undetected drift to the 60 pages that pass; instead, exactly two structurally atypical page KINDS carry overrides (the one-page styleguide and the image-bearing product pages). Overrides are page-kind-scoped, never per-page escape hatches: a third candidate means the default is wrong or the page is doing too much — escalate to the product-owner, do not add a line. maxCssBundleBytes hard-caps the built sass/main.min.*.css: under single-bundle architecture every CSS byte multiplies across all 64 pages, so bundle growth is gated at its named cause instead of surfacing as scattered page-budget breaches (same hard-max pattern as the font gates in tool/subset_fonts.sh). Revisit triggers: the styleguide override dies if the component library is ever split across routes; the notably override is contingent on current image encoding — a screenshot re-encode tripping 125,000 is deliberate, not a flaky gate. All six numbers ratchet-down-only from the merge commit forward. Ratchet applied 2026-07-26 (scroll fade-in system removed at Ivan's direction: fade.js, its CSS, the data-js stamp — ~800-950 B/page + 348 B bundle): 123,000 → 122,000 default, styleguide 130,000 → 129,000, notably 125,000 → 124,000, bundle 35,000 → 34,600 — same margin methodology as the 2026-07-26 product-owner ruling (8% over heaviest regular page 112,894; ~1.7%/~1.3% over the override kinds' worst; ~1.2 KB bundle headroom). Product-owner ruling 2026-07-27 (design-review phase): maxCssBundleBytes raised 34,600 -> 52,000 as an INTERIM cap for Ivan's iterative UI-fidelity review, in which whole pages are rebuilt round by round (home landed first at 42,102 B, +8,103). The 10,000 B of headroom is a test, not padding: the home round created the shared vocabulary (section-title, pricing comparison table, service rail, news rows, join band) that the remaining rounds consume, so services+news+about together must cost less than home alone did — if the cap trips, the cause is a duplicated or unharvested layer, investigate before raising. Ratchet-down is SUSPENDED for this number during the review phase only; reductions are banked to the revert recalibration, never taken as slack. This cap expires at temp-skin revert; a review that closes without a clean revert needs a fresh ruling. Every rebuild round MUST (1) harvest dead CSS in the same commit and (2) report projected post-revert page weight — heaviest page + 43,864 B, the uniform font delta from restoring Fraunces (32,864) + Karla (26,764) and dropping Bellefair (15,764), which lands raw and per-page because tool/serve.mjs does not compress and head.html preloads both faces everywhere. That projection is a reported number, never a gate: it must not block a design round. As of the home round it already breaches (91,908 -> 135,772 vs the 129,000 styleguide override), which is why it is tracked while fixes are still cheap. At skin revert ALL SIX numbers recalibrate on measured weights and ratchet discipline resumes; if the projection still breaches, the ranked options are trim/harvest first, font load second (brand decision — routes to the brand owners, never pulled to make a gate pass), raising the numbers LAST and only for structure explicitly approved. Never delete the maxCssBundleBytes key to unblock a push — check_page_budget.mjs skips the check entirely when it is absent.

/styleguide/.justification: The template's deliberate kitchen-sink demo: the entire component library, including the permanent contact-form demo, on ONE page by design. Contingent on the styleguide staying a single page (product-owner ruling 2026-07-26).

/fr-fr/styleguide/.justification: Same as /styleguide/, FR copy — EN/FR delta is translation noise, never encoded in the numbers.

/products/notably/.justification: Product detail page renders a real product screenshot via the figure pipeline (AVIF/WebP/srcset) — image-bearing by design, per the ratchet policy. 120,000 → 125,000 with the single-bundle restructure (+~7.7 KB/page site-wide); relative headroom TIGHTENED versus mechanically preserving the old margin (product-owner ruling 2026-07-26).
